## Answer Key: Chapter 5 {#sec-solutions-ch5 .unnumbered}

Full solutions to Chapter 5's "Check your understanding" questions
(@sec-ch5).

**1. Explain.** *Answer.* Dense: every token uses the same feed-forward
parameters. MoE: a router selects top-$k$ of $E$ experts per token;
only the selected experts run.

**2. Explain.** *Answer.* Active model parameters include $p_{\text{base}}$
(and $p_s$, if any) which stay active regardless of routing; active
*bank* parameters ($k p_e$) count only the routed experts.

**3. Compare.** *Answer.* No. MoE sparsity is *which parameters* activate
(feed-forward); sparse attention (Ch. 4) is *which positions* are
scored. Orthogonal axes.

**4. Misconception check.** *Answer.* False, unless restricted to the
routed bank. $p_{\text{base}}$/$p_s$ stay active, so the whole-model
ratio is always closer to 1 than $E/k$.

**5. Misconception check.** *Answer.* False. Unselected experts are
still stored weights that must fit in memory -- sparsity affects
compute, not storage. *Common trap:* equating "not activated" with
"not stored."

**6. Calculation.** *Answer.* Bank: total $=16{\times}50\text{M}=800\text{M}$,
active $=4{\times}50\text{M}=200\text{M}$, ratio $4.0$. Model: total
$=2\text{B}+800\text{M}=2.8\text{B}$, active $=2\text{B}+200\text{M}=2.2\text{B}$,
ratio $\approx 1.27$ (verified programmatically).

**7. Design exercise (applied exercise).** *Answer.* The MoE model has
the larger serving memory footprint. The certain fact: serving memory
must hold (most of) *total* parameters regardless of which are active
for any one token, and a MoE model's total is by construction larger
than its active count -- while the dense model's total equals its
active count exactly. *Interview criteria:* does the answer name this
structural fact rather than guessing from typical model sizes?

**8. Interview practice.** *Answer.* 2/64 tells you the *routed bank's*
activation ratio only. It does not tell you: the whole model's
total/active ratio (base/shared parameters are unaffected); exact
FLOPs (routing and combination cost something too); memory footprint
(all 64 experts are still stored); or communication cost (depends on
how routing actually lands across devices, not on $k$/$E$ alone).
*Interview criteria:* does the answer address all four (parameters,
FLOPs, memory, communication) rather than stopping after one or two?
